I get that they're trying to be the wave of the future or something, but this is incredibly stupid. Why would you subject yourself to a medical procedure with all the attendant risks and problems that carries instead of simply issuing NFC/RFID tags? It's not as though someone couldn't circumvent this by cloning a tag, then you're stuck having to get the thing yanked out of your hand. Did they think none of their employees were ever going to need an MRI, ever?

I've always been skeptical of implantable tech, as nobody has come close to solving the issue of obsolescence. Until they do, it's either a fad, a bad choice, or both.

While I agree convincing your employees to implant tech is remarkably dumb, I am optimistic about the future of this technology. I think implantable technology is fascinating because humanity is finally reaching a period of unprecedented augmentation. I want to see ultraviolet in my lifetime and hear above 20,000 Hz. I recognize these fantasies are unnecessary and dangerous, but I hope one day the reward will outweigh the risks.

I think that'll depend on our eventual ability to mitigate surgical risks. Perhaps when we can create fake eyes that offer a better experience than real ones, we'll be well past the point where it's a big deal to crack your head open, rip out your eyes and hook new ones into your brain. As it stands, even the relatively minimally invasive procedure they're doing in the OP example presents risks of infection, allergic reactions or other unplanned outcomes - and that's not even getting into the complications from the inevitable removal of the device.

Yes the surgical risk of this "grain of rice" is still undeniable. I'm just pointing out that I welcome crazy people paving the way for a future technology I support. In this case there were several layers of irresponsibility, namely privacy concerns, and the inevitable removal you mentioned when the employee no longer works for this company. Howerver, I hope you'll agree the more surgeries like this that occur, the more we can learn about how to minimize those surgical risks.
